parole.testo: From English arsenic, from Latin arsenicum, from Ancient Greek ἀρσενικόν (arsenikón, “yellow arsenic”). Ultimately a doublet of rëzëgojë (originally *ërsingë), which seems to have been borrowed from Ancient Greek directly, as well as a doublet of klor (“chlorine“).
Probably from English genitive, or a learned borrowing from Latin genitīvus (“pertaining to origin, birth”), genetīvus, from genitus (perfect passive participle of gignō (“beget”)).
